11 / The story · The land

North of the Ganga, a plain made by rivers.

Mithila is river country: ponds, fish, lotus, and the litchi orchards of Vaishali and Muzaffarpur. The fish on our bottle is the old sign of this region.

12 / The story · The republic

7,707 rajas. No king.

From about the 7th century BCE the Licchavi clans ruled themselves from Vaishali. Tradition counts 7,707 heads of families in their Assembly, which met each spring, and a council of nine that answered to it. The republic fell to Magadha around 468 BCE.

Historians call it an aristocratic republic. The seats were inherited, not elected.

13 / The story · The craft

Drink was a craft here long before gin.

The Arthashastra, the ancient Indian manual of statecraft, lists the drinks of its day: medaka from rice, asava from wood-apple, sugar and honey, maireya spiced with pepper, madhu from grapes. In the villages, palms were tapped for toddy and mahua flowers were gathered.

Bihar has been a dry state since 2016, so Litchvi will be distilled under licence elsewhere in India.

14 / The story · The hands

The women of Mithila painted their walls.

For generations they have painted their homes by hand: fish for prosperity, lotus for purity, peacocks for love. That hand is on every Litchvi bottle.

01 / The lead botanical

Shahi litchi. The heart of it.

Grown in Muzaffarpur, Vaishali and the districts around them, Shahi litchi has carried a GI tag since 2018. In Litchvi it gives the gin its floral fruit and a soft, rounded middle.

25 g per litre of spirit01 / 09

The Shahi name goes on the bottle only when the fruit comes from authorised growers.

02 / The flesh

Tear the skin. Keep the perfume.

What the flesh brings to the glass: rose and litchi blossom on the nose, a gentle sweetness on the tongue, a long clean finish. Then it goes into copper.

Flavour notes only. Indian food law allows no health claims for alcohol.

03 / Nine botanicals

Nine botanicals. None of them rules.

Juniper berry02 / 09
The piney backbone. Without it, it is not gin.
22 g per litre of spirit

04 / Copper and rest

One slow run. Then two weeks of quiet.

Twelve to sixteen hours of maceration, one run through copper, and only the heart of the spirit is kept.

00days rested of 14 · bottled at 42.8% v/v

Gin takes its flavour from botanicals, not from wood, so it is not an aged spirit. It rests so the flavours settle, then it is bottled.

05 / First pour

Poured first into a piala.

A shallow black cup with a hammered brass rim. It is our tribute to the Licchavi table, where no one sat above another.

A tribute, not a relic. We make no claim about what the Licchavis drank.
